chapter: Sounds and recording in old New Orleans
title: Recording technology then and now
summary: Alcorn compares thin early microphones with modern multi-track recording, and mentions old records made in dance halls.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Do you think there's something about music today that, in a way, compensates for the loss of sound? Or the things that work to the advantage of a musician that you didn't have many years ago?

Well, yes. Every year they improve upon things. You take thirds and record it. I know I recorded it. I have a record that I recorded at 37. It sounded good, yeah. Mm-hmm. And it was made in the thirties. But they didn't have all the mic systems back there. A couple of mics didn't do it. Now they got everything. Back in the room in the hotel and records. You see? That's nice. Equipment wasn't picking up like it. It was made a good song. It was the Sammy Lewis records. They're back in the English. Yeah.
A lot of the Hot Five records are good today. Good today.
From that sound. But if they recorded it, they're looking for Sammy there. But they didn't prove it on the sound. Yeah. Put everybody on a different track. Sure.
I guess it really gives you a better sense of all the harmony. Sure.

But not today. I mean, back in the old days people just had the night or summer record play. They would go in the old dance hall and record. Not record you command, the guy command. You can do anything to take. 40 years they put it out. I got a record like that. We made it in the Pedder. It sounded very bad. Down in the French court?

Yeah. But a guy came in a Pedder. I can remember. Sometime he got a tape in the 80s and released him. The office picked him or something like that. But you could see where he had something. But it would have been better if it had been recorded. You know, that's the guy had mics and everything. They took him one of them and went to the world for a long distance. Wow.
